@graph.name: O.A.S.I.S. glossary
@graph.description: Plain definitions of the terms used across the O.A.S.I.S. product, website and Journal.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Embedding
hasDefinedTerm.description: A numeric representation of meaning. It lets the assistant compare pieces of text by what they mean, not just the words used.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Inference
hasDefinedTerm.description: The moment a model actually produces an answer from your input. On a local assistant it happens on your PC, using your CPU or GPU.

hasDefinedTerm.name: LLM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Large Language Model — the kind of AI model that reads and writes text. Local models are smaller versions you can run yourself.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Local AI
hasDefinedTerm.description: An AI assistant that runs its model on your own computer instead of sending your data to a server. You keep control of the model and the files.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Local inference
hasDefinedTerm.description: Running the AI model on your own hardware, rather than on a remote server. The response is produced on your machine.

hasDefinedTerm.name: OCR
hasDefinedTerm.description: Optical Character Recognition — reading text out of an image or a screenshot so the assistant can act on it or copy it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: On-device
hasDefinedTerm.description: Work handled by your own computer's hardware instead of a remote server. Audio, images and text never have to leave the machine.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Semantic search
hasDefinedTerm.description: Search that looks for meaning and related concepts rather than only exact words. Useful when you remember the idea but not the wording.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Speech recognition
hasDefinedTerm.description: Turning your spoken words into text. O.A.S.I.S. does this on your PC, so dictation works without sending audio anywhere.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Speech synthesis
hasDefinedTerm.description: Turning text into spoken audio. It lets the assistant answer out loud, in Spanish or English, using voices on your machine.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Vision
hasDefinedTerm.description: The ability to look at an image or your screen and describe what is there. It only happens when you ask.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Voice cloning
hasDefinedTerm.description: Building a synthetic voice from a sample so replies sound like a chosen speaker. A Max feature, created from audio you provide yourself.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Wake word
hasDefinedTerm.description: A short phrase that starts listening without touching the keyboard. Recognition runs locally, so the microphone is not streamed anywhere.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Context window
hasDefinedTerm.description: How much text the model can consider at once. Larger windows let it handle longer documents and conversations.

hasDefinedTerm.name: GGUF
hasDefinedTerm.description: A model file format commonly used for running AI models locally. It packages a model into a single file your PC can load.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Hugging Face
hasDefinedTerm.description: A large public catalogue of AI models. The app searches it so you can pick a compatible model and download it without hunting for files.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Model
hasDefinedTerm.description: The AI 'brain' — a large file that has learned patterns from text. You download one and it runs on your computer.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Quantization
hasDefinedTerm.description: A way of compressing a model so it uses less memory and runs faster, at a small cost in quality. Q4 is a common middle ground.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Token
hasDefinedTerm.description: A small chunk of text — roughly part of a word — that the model reads and writes. Speed is usually measured in tokens per second.

hasDefinedTerm.name: CPU
hasDefinedTerm.description: The main processor of your computer. It can run small AI models on its own, just more slowly than a graphics card.

hasDefinedTerm.name: GPU
hasDefinedTerm.description: A graphics card. For AI it acts as an accelerator, producing answers noticeably faster than the CPU alone.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Model size
hasDefinedTerm.description: Usually written like '7B' — billions of parameters. Bigger models know more but need more memory and run slower.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Offloading
hasDefinedTerm.description: Splitting a model between your graphics card and your processor so it fits in the memory you have available.

hasDefinedTerm.name: RAM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Your computer's working memory. It holds the model while it runs, so more RAM lets you load larger models.

hasDefinedTerm.name: VRAM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Memory available on a graphics card. Larger local models generally need more VRAM when running on the GPU.

hasDefinedTerm.name: API
hasDefinedTerm.description: A defined way for two programs to talk to each other. Here it usually means the local interface other tools use to reach O.A.S.I.S.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Docker
hasDefinedTerm.description: A tool that runs software in isolated containers. O.A.S.I.S. uses it to execute generated code safely, and it is optional.

hasDefinedTerm.name: EULA
hasDefinedTerm.description: End User Licence Agreement — the terms you accept to install and use the app. It ships with the installer and covers one Windows machine.

hasDefinedTerm.name: llama.cpp
hasDefinedTerm.description: A widely used local runtime that loads GGUF models and runs them efficiently on CPUs and GPUs. It is the engine under many local AI tools.

hasDefinedTerm.name: LM Studio
hasDefinedTerm.description: A desktop app for downloading and chatting with local models. Excellent for a chat window; it does not drive your PC or keep a memory of you.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Local database
hasDefinedTerm.description: The file on your disk where memory is stored — messages, notes and documents, indexed so they can be found again by meaning.

hasDefinedTerm.name: MCP
hasDefinedTerm.description: A protocol that lets AI systems connect to external tools and services in a standardised way. It is how O.A.S.I.S. can use outside tool servers.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Ollama
hasDefinedTerm.description: A popular way to run local models from a command line. It is strong as a model server; O.A.S.I.S. is the assistant layer around a model.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Open source
hasDefinedTerm.description: Software whose source code is published for anyone to read and modify. O.A.S.I.S. is not: it is proprietary, with a public changelog instead.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Proprietary
hasDefinedTerm.description: Software whose source code is not public and is licensed by its owner. The app is proprietary; the AI models you run are licensed separately.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Repository
hasDefinedTerm.description: The public project folder on GitHub, where releases, the roadmap and the changelog live.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Runtime
hasDefinedTerm.description: The engine that actually loads a model file and produces answers. It is what turns a downloaded file into a working assistant.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SHA-256 hash
hasDefinedTerm.description: A short fingerprint of a file. Comparing it with the published value proves the installer you downloaded is the one that was released.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Tool server
hasDefinedTerm.description: An external service that offers extra tools to the assistant. You add it yourself, so it only runs when you configure it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Action log
hasDefinedTerm.description: A local record of what the assistant did, kept on your machine so you can review or undo recent actions.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Analytics
hasDefinedTerm.description: Scripts that count visitors and behaviour. This site runs none, and the app has no analytics built in — there is nothing to opt out of.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Encryption
hasDefinedTerm.description: Scrambling stored data so only someone with the key can read it. Secrets and the local vault are encrypted on your machine.

hasDefinedTerm.name: High-impact action
hasDefinedTerm.description: An action that can change or remove things — like deleting files, running code or shutting down. These always ask for confirmation first.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Isolation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Keeping an action inside its own contained environment, with limits on what it can read, write or reach.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Permission
hasDefinedTerm.description: Your per-tool setting that decides whether an action runs automatically, asks first, or is blocked. You can change it at any time.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Sandbox
hasDefinedTerm.description: An isolated environment used to run code with additional safety boundaries, so generated code cannot reach the rest of your system.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Telemetry
hasDefinedTerm.description: Usage or crash data sent back to the maker. Here it ships off: nothing is reported unless you deliberately enable an outbound channel.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Vault
hasDefinedTerm.description: The encrypted store for secrets such as API keys and tokens. It lives on your disk, not in a cloud account or a plain config file.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cloud
hasDefinedTerm.description: Computing that runs on someone else's servers over the internet. Here it is the alternative the app is built to avoid for everyday tasks.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Endpoint
hasDefinedTerm.description: A specific address a program can send requests to. With telemetry off, there is no endpoint receiving your data by default.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Integration
hasDefinedTerm.description: A connection to an outside service, like a messaging platform. It only communicates when you enable and use it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Localhost
hasDefinedTerm.description: Your own machine as seen by itself. The app's internal server listens there, so nothing is exposed on your network.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Network features
hasDefinedTerm.description: The optional parts that reach the internet, such as web search and integrations. They only communicate when you use or configure them.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Server
hasDefinedTerm.description: A remote computer that answers requests. A local assistant avoids depending on one for chat, voice or memory.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Webhook
hasDefinedTerm.description: A URL that receives a message when something happens. O.A.S.I.S. only uses one if you set it up for diagnostics.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Agent
hasDefinedTerm.description: An assistant that does more than answer: it plans, uses tools, asks for permission and verifies the result.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Browser extension
hasDefinedTerm.description: A Max add-on that lets the browser talk to your assistant on the same PC, so it can work with the page you are looking at.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Companion
hasDefinedTerm.description: Optional apps that reach your assistant from elsewhere — phone, browser or chat platforms — over your own network.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Local-first
hasDefinedTerm.description: Designed to keep local tasks and data on your PC, while still allowing optional network-enabled features when you choose to use them.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Max
hasDefinedTerm.description: The paid edition: advanced coding, sandboxed execution, workflows, integrations and companion apps. A one-time payment, not a subscription.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Memory
hasDefinedTerm.description: What the assistant keeps between conversations — facts, notes and documents — stored on your disk and searchable by meaning.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Offline
hasDefinedTerm.description: Supported local features can work without internet after a model is downloaded. Network-enabled features require connectivity when used.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Offline-first
hasDefinedTerm.description: Built so the core experience works without a connection, and network access is an extra you opt into — not a requirement to function.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Persistent memory
hasDefinedTerm.description: Information that survives after the conversation ends, so you don't have to repeat yourself every time.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Personal
hasDefinedTerm.description: The free plan: local chat, voice, memory, documents and everyday PC control, with no account and no message limits.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Skill
hasDefinedTerm.description: A small piece of behaviour triggered by your phrases, so common requests get handled your way.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Tool
hasDefinedTerm.description: A single capability the assistant can use — reading a file, changing the volume, setting a timer — each with its own permission level.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Workflow
hasDefinedTerm.description: A routine you describe in plain words, like 'every day at 9 send me a briefing', that runs on a schedule.
